pattern: Using playful consumer colors for enterprise SaaS
why: Undermines trust and professional appearance
instead: Use professional blues, slate, and controlled accent colors

pattern: Overly complex dashboard on first load
why: Overwhelms new users before they learn the product
instead: Use progressive disclosure: start simple, reveal complexity as needed

pattern: AI purple/pink gradients for serious B2B tools
why: Feels amateurish and undermines enterprise credibility
instead: Use professional color palette matching the product domain

pattern: Playful or neon colors for financial platforms
why: Reduces trust in financial applications
instead: Use conservative blues, greens, and controlled accent colors

pattern: Hiding security badges and compliance info
why: Users need to see security signals in financial contexts
instead: Display trust signals prominently in checkout and account areas

pattern: Complex navigation for trading platforms
why: Trading requires speed; complex nav slows decision-making
instead: Use persistent top-level navigation for key trading functions

pattern: Low contrast text on medical interfaces
why: Healthcare users often have visual impairments or are reading under stress
instead: Always exceed WCAG AA (4.5:1) minimum contrast

pattern: Decorative animations on medical interfaces
why: Creates distraction in high-stakes environments
instead: Minimize motion; use static, clear information displays

pattern: Lighthearted consumer design for clinical tools
why: Healthcare professionals need serious, data-dense interfaces
instead: Use clean, professional design with clear information hierarchy

pattern: Hidden shipping costs until checkout
why: Major cause of cart abandonment and trust loss
instead: Show estimated total including shipping early in the flow

pattern: Too many competing CTAs on product pages
why: Analysis paralysis reduces conversion rates
instead: One primary CTA (Add to Cart) with secondary actions clearly subordinate

pattern: Auto-playing videos or carousels
why: Annoying to users, hurts accessibility, and can slow the page
instead: Use user-initiated video/carousel controls

pattern: Generic stock photography for service businesses
why: Reduces authenticity and trust in service providers
instead: Use real photos of the team, space, and actual work

pattern: Long forms without progress indication
why: Users abandon multi-step service forms without visible progress
instead: Use stepper or progress bar for multi-step forms

pattern: Hard-to-find contact information
why: Service customers often need to contact the business quickly
instead: Make phone, email, and chat prominently available

pattern: Overly corporate design for creative portfolios
why: Fails to express the creative individual or agency's personality
instead: Use bold typography, experimental layouts, and personal expression

pattern: Slow-loading portfolio with heavy images
why: Potential clients will leave before seeing the work
instead: Optimize images, lazy-load, and show thumbnails first

pattern: Templated, cookie-cutter design for creative brands
why: Fails to differentiate the creative professional from competitors
instead: Use unique layout, custom illustrations, and distinctive typography

pattern: Overly complex UI for simple habit tracking
why: Users want quick input; complex UI reduces consistency
instead: Minimal input with one-tap logging for daily habits

pattern: Too much friction in journaling/diary apps
why: High friction reduces writing frequency
instead: Quick entry mode, templates, and reminders

pattern: Gamification that feels manipulative
why: Users can sense when gamification serves the app, not them
instead: Meaningful progress indicators that genuinely help the user

pattern: Over-hyped design language (too much neon, glitch, cyber)
why: Looks dated quickly and can feel gimmicky
instead: Balance futuristic elements with clean, usable design

pattern: Complexity that hides core functionality
why: Cutting-edge tech is already complex; UI should simplify
instead: Progressive disclosure: simple interface with advanced options accessible

pattern: Ignoring accessibility in 'futuristic' UIs
why: Emerging tech should be inclusive from the start
instead: Apply accessibility standards even to experimental interfaces

pattern: Pure black (#000) background with pure white (#FFF) text
why: Causes eye strain from extreme contrast on dark mode
instead: Use dark gray (#1a1a2e or similar) background with off-white text

pattern: Text over complex glass backgrounds without sufficient contrast
why: Becomes unreadable, especially in varying lighting conditions
instead: Ensure text contrast passes WCAG AA over frosted backgrounds

pattern: Interactive elements that look identical to non-interactive ones
why: Users can't tell what's clickable
instead: Use distinct visual treatment for interactive vs static elements

pattern: Childish appearance for serious applications
why: Undermines credibility of professional tools
instead: Use claymorphism only for appropriate audiences (kids, creative, wellness)

pattern: Confusing navigation in brutalist design
why: Brutalism's raw aesthetic can sacrifice usability
instead: Maintain clear navigation even within raw aesthetic

pattern: No visual hierarchy due to complete flatness
why: Users can't distinguish interactive elements from static content
instead: Use color, spacing, and typography to create hierarchy without shadows
